throughput.what_a_day_buys: The record says one working day with one clear ruling from Aaron produces a finished, gated, shipped piece the same day, usually with its before-and-after board and two or three side fixes nobody asked for. The measured pace across the two build periods is 1.5 to 2.2 tracker rows closed per changelog day and 3.7 to 4.75 changelog entries per changelog day, with 20 to 40 commits on a working day. Three examples from the record. One: 2026-08-24, the two-control HUD. Aaron ruled on 08-22, 'A, the symbol; roomy inset; 64px on desktop; spent states approved' (TODO.md row 103 note). Two days later the HUD shipped as ruled: pause and replay only, the phone's three-dot tray and its four proxy buttons deleted, replay painted grey or orange by state, fixes 108 and 109 (the pause-road bugs) closed with it, hud-check 24 checks with three sabotages, pause-paths-check rewritten to 35 checks, a before/after artifact at both viewports (BUILD.md line 5483). The same day the list got its ruled order (36 rows re-sorted, 17 moved) and the whole post-launch design became rows 112 to 124; five changelog entries on 08-24. Two: 2026-09-04, the entrance. Aaron said 'Let me just see what you got with one of the hardwood themes so I can visualize better. Build it and let me see it in game.' By that evening the tunnel push, the sky-to-court drop and the ref between the squads were in the game for every court family with cine-check at 21 checks and 45 gates green; his catch 'the tunnel should happen after this screen' was moved the same turn; two option boards (the referee piece, the drop) were rendered by the game itself; he picked 'for ref, do 4 on phone and 1 on desktop' and 'go with 1 build it', and the opening was rebuilt end to end that night, closing rows 215 and 217 to 222 with cine-check at 38 checks (BUILD.md lines 4185 to 4287). `git log` shows 9 commits dated 09-04; seven rows closed in one day, and the lot went live on 09-05 on 'lets ship everything live.' Three: 2026-09-07, the possession mock-up. Aaron's pushback on 09-06 was 'still a lot of jargon and unclear stuff... walk me through from tip off'. On 09-07 he got the plain-language walkthrough page, answered twelve decisions by voice, ruled B, C and D ('For the other three I'll go with your recommendations'), ruled the big man ('b, go with the count'), and said 'Done, don't worry about the feedback, let's get the clickable mockup'. The same day the new turn engine landed as docs/play/flow.js behind ?flow=new with every ruled sentence playing on the real court, flow-check 20 checks and a two-minute machine run (BUILD.md lines 4032 to 4107); six commits dated 09-07, five changelog entries, rows 245 and 246 ruled and built. Two more days of the same shape: 08-28 (nine blocks, rows 206, 207, 128, 127, 129 and 195 shipped after his one-line order ruling) and 08-31 (rows 13, 214 and 213 shipped and the five practice flags answered after 'go ahead and build'). The flip side is also measured: a ruling that asks for another ruling buys nothing. Row 15 ruled 08-11 is still open; the 10-18 deadline produced one commit and then 18 days of nothing because the cut it depended on was never ruled. So for the fourteen days: each day Aaron opens with one buildable ruling is worth, on the record, about two closed rows and a shipped piece with its gate; each day that opens waiting on him is worth zero.

verdicts.arithmetic: THE DAYS. Fourteen calendar days; day 1 is the scope pick, day 14 the merge and the link, so 12 days are buildable (python3: 14-2 = 12). The project's measured quiet days are 2 of 16 (Track B) and 5 of 24 (gameplay rebuild): 7/40 = 0.175, and 12 * (1 - 7/40) = 9.90 working days. That 9.9 is the scope's own number and it recomputes. The scope's "fits" rows sum to 9.75 (2.5 + 2.5 + 1 + 2.5 + 5 * 0.25; python3 printed 9.75), so the slack is 9.90 - 9.75 = 0.15 of a working day, which is 1.2 hours of an 8-hour day. The "does not fit" rows sum to 19 (9 * 1 + 5 + 5), all twenty rows to 28.75, and the scope's own split checks: 27-items 18.5 (16, 15, 17, 19, 21, 20) plus live bugs 10.25. So the build-days claim is true by 1.2 hours, with zero room for one extra quiet day, one failed option round, or one bug that takes a half day longer than its quarter. THE QUIET DAYS ARE COUNTED TWICE DIFFERENTLY. The scope deducts quiet days from the build (9.9 of 12) but not from the bank: it counts "thirteen data days" of fourteen, which assumes data work on day 1 and day 14 and zero quiet days. At the build's own rate 13 * 0.825 = 10.7 data days. The scope's "would start day N" column also ignores quiet days: row 20 at "day 26" is day 2 + 23.75 build days with no quiet; at the measured rate it is day 2 + 23.75/0.825 = day 30.8, and the full 28.75 days of all twenty rows is 34.8 calendar days before day 1 and the merge are added. THE GATE SUM DOES NOT RECOMPUTE. The scope states "reads at 21 a day plus 38 kept cards a day" and "317 + 246 + 494 = 1,057" over thirteen days. 38 * 13 = 494 holds, but 21 * 13 = 273, not 246; 246/13 = 18.92 reads a day. With the stated 21 + 38 the thirteen-day total is 1,084 and twelve days give 1,025, not "exactly 1,000"; the "exactly 1,000" is only true at 18.92 + 38 = 56.92 a day over twelve days (python3: 12 * 56.92 + 317 = 1000). Whichever rate is meant, the sum printed in the scope does not match the rate printed beside it. Under the build's own quiet rate the gate misses: 10.7 data days give 317 + 225 + 407 = 948; 9.9 give 901. The gap to close is 1,000 - 317 = 683 cards, which is 52.5 a day over 13 days, 63.8 over 10.7, 69.0 over 9.9. `python3 tools/gate-blockers.py` today: DEALABLE TODAY 317, GATE TARGET 1000, "317 dealable + 290 readable = 607 best case from verification alone", "realistic: 393 more cards needed beyond the readable ones". The writing pace has never been measured as dealable cards: `git grep -hoE '(dateChecked|date_checked)...' 7262864 -- docs/*` counts stamps by month 2026-07 594, 2026-08 411, and the last five stamp dates are 08-04 154, 08-05 194, 08-06 49, 08-07 12, 08-12 2; nothing since, 85 days ago (python3 date arithmetic). The 411 August stamps over 12 days were 34.2 a day on existing cards, the only measured stamping pace in the record, and 08-07 to 08-12 managed 14. `python3 tools/diversity.py`: "THIN every era present 6 below 5 (scales to 15 at 1,000): 1930s, 1950s, 1960s, 1970s, nba-1940s, nba-1950s", 7 of 8 pass, 318 cards. THE RULING LAG. The throughput report's measured lag for a buildable ruling is median 0, mean 0.6 days, 9 of 13 same day; that part of the schedule is sound for days 2 to 11 IF Aaron is present. The failure mode in the record is the ruling that needs another ruling: 10-18 to 11-01 is 14 days (python3) with 0 commits, and `git log --all --since=2026-09-15 --format=%ad | sort | uniq -c` prints 4 on 10-09, 1 on 10-18, 2 on 11-05 (this workflow's own commits b2171d8 and 2a8a356; HEAD is now 2a8a356, not 7262864). This scope stacks five rulings on day 1: the scope pick, the new date, the bank rule, whether a spine-mined card is dealable the day it is written, and whether the twenty get the link without row 21 and row 20. Two of those ask him to overrule himself (the five pulled forward; the gym). The recent quiet rate is 50 of 52 days; at that rate 12 days hold 0.46 working days. The 9.9 assumes his August pace returns on day 2. THE MERGE. `git rev-list --count main..HEAD` = 26 and `git merge-base main HEAD` equals main, so the fast-forward is real (it was 24 at 7262864; today's two commits made it 26). One day for the merge, Pages verification and the link is in line with 08-30 and 09-05. VERDICT: the build half fits by 1.2 hours with no buffer; the gate half fits only on a calendar that has no quiet days and a rate whose own sum is wrong; the day-1 stack is the kind of ruling the record says waits indefinitely. Not feasible as stated.
